# Maglev

> Maglev is a free, open source Android app that downloads almost any link. Paste or share a YouTube, X (Twitter) or Instagram video link, a file, a magnet link or a .torrent file, and Maglev gets it, with a quality picker for videos and pause and resume for everything. It also has a browser that finds videos on a page, search across torrent sources, feeds and subtitles. No ads, no tracking, no account. Android 7 and later. Version 1.1.

Made by Harsh Dayal (https://harshdayal.dev, GitHub: https://github.com/Kaos599). License: GPL-3.0.

## Video sites

- Maglev downloads YouTube videos and Shorts, Instagram Reels and videos, and X (Twitter) videos on Android.
- Share or paste a YouTube, X or Instagram link. Reddit, Vimeo and TikTok links are recognised too. Maglev reads the video with yt-dlp on the phone and shows up to 6 qualities. You pick one, and it downloads with pause and resume into Download/Maglev.
- In Maglev's browser, long-press a video on YouTube, X or Instagram and choose Download.
- yt-dlp updates itself once a day on Wi-Fi. In Settings > Updates > Video sites you can turn this off or allow mobile data.
- A video behind a sign-in (private accounts, many Instagram posts, age-gated videos) may not download. Maglev says "needs sign-in". Public Reels and posts are the ones that can work.
- Maglev never gets around DRM. Live streams and protected video can't be saved.
- Maglev is free, open source (GPL-3.0), has no ads, no tracking and no account, and needs Android 7 or later. The arm64 APK is about 43 MB because Python and yt-dlp are bundled.
- Install from GitHub releases or with Obtainium. Maglev is not on Google Play.
- Download only what you have the right to.
- [YouTube downloader for Android](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/youtube-downloader-android): Maglev is a free, open source YouTube downloader for Android. Share or paste a YouTube video or Shorts link, and Maglev reads it with yt-dlp on your phone and shows up to 6 qualities. Pick one and it downloads, with pause and resume, into Download/Maglev. No ads, no account.
- [Instagram Reels downloader for Android](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/instagram-reels-downloader): Maglev is a free, open source Instagram Reels downloader for Android. Share or paste the link of a public Reel or video, and Maglev reads it with yt-dlp on your phone and shows up to 6 qualities. Pick one and it downloads into Download/Maglev. Posts that need a sign-in may not download.
- [X (Twitter) video downloader for Android](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/twitter-video-downloader): Maglev is a free, open source X (Twitter) video downloader for Android. Share or paste the link of a post with a video, and Maglev reads it with yt-dlp on your phone and shows up to 6 qualities. Pick one and it downloads into Download/Maglev. Videos that need a sign-in may not download.

## Key facts

- Every download in one list: Torrents, files and videos sit in the same list, each with its size, progress, speed and time left, such as 412 MB of 1.2 GB. A queue decides how many run at once. Pause, resume and retry survive a restart, and downloads keep going with the screen off. One + button for a link you paste or type, a .torrent file, Search or the browser. Paste or share a YouTube, X, Instagram or other video link, then pick a quality (Video sites). Share a magnet, a .torrent file or a file link to Maglev from any app, or open .torrent files from your file manager. Transfers says why a download is held (Wi-Fi only, battery, schedule, storage full and more), with a button to change that setting. Swipe a row right to pause or resume it, or left to remove it from the list (files are kept). You can turn this off. A file type icon on each card (a torrent's comes from its biggest file), which you can turn off. Play a video while it downloads, from its card or its screen. Open any download's folder in one tap, and share a finished file. On mobile data, the add screen shows the size before you start. Pause all, Resume all and Shut down from the notification. A live chip in the status bar on Android 16 and later. Unknown times show as unknown, never guessed.
- A browser that blocks ads and finds the files on a page: Open any page inside Maglev. Ads and trackers are blocked before they load. Play a video and Maglev lists it, together with the page's other files, in a tray you can filter by type. Tap one to download it with the page's cookies, so files behind a sign-in still work. Over 42,000 blocked domains from StevenBlack/hosts, refreshed once a day on its own. Add your own lists and they refresh too. Tabs with a long-press menu on links and images: new tab, background tab, copy, share or download. Pop-ups and redirects you didn't tap for wait until you choose Open, Block or Always allow on this site. Find in page and text size. A history you can search, with suggestions as you type and recent pages on every new tab. It can clear itself when you close Maglev. App installers come with a warning. Swipe the address bar left or right to switch tabs, or down to see all tabs. Downloads that start without a tap go to the found-files tray instead, pages can't fill your Back history to keep you on them, known crypto-mining scripts are blocked, and pages open over HTTPS when the site supports it.
- Streaming video, saved as one file: Many sites play video as hundreds of small pieces listed in a playlist: HLS (.m3u8) or DASH. Maglev reads the playlist, lets you pick the quality and audio language, downloads the pieces and joins them into one video file. On-demand HLS and DASH, including HLS with standard AES-128 encryption. DRM-protected video and live streams are refused, and Maglev says why. Separate video and audio are joined without re-encoding.
- Subtitles for the videos you download: Open a finished download, or a video inside a torrent, and tap Find subtitles. Maglev asks 21 free sources, with no account, and groups what it finds as Fits this file, Probably fits and May be out of sync. The subtitle is saved next to the video, so your player picks it up. Open a finished link download's menu in Transfers, a torrent's options, or the ⋯ next to a video in its Files tab. Saved as <video name>.<lang>.srt (or .ass or .vtt). If that name exists, you choose Replace or Keep both. Pick and order languages, set a hearing-impaired preference and turn each source on or off in Settings > Finding things > Subtitle sources. Two sources match by file fingerprint: Subtis for Spanish and Napisy24 for Polish. The rest match by name, so check the fit. The source list updates itself from Maglev's signed list. Nothing is looked up until you tap Find subtitles.
- One search, many sources, one list: Type once and Maglev asks up to 40 built-in public torrent indexes at the same time, including ones you can switch off by category. Results that point to the same torrent are merged, so you see one row with every source that has it. Filter results by category, and sort by seeders, size or date. A size range slider hides results that are too small or too big. 40 built-in sources; choose which answer each category. Source addresses update once a day from a signed list, so a source that moves keeps working without an app update. Add your own Jackett or Prowlarr indexer. Sources known for fake uploads carry a warning.
- Feeds that download new episodes for you: Follow a show from Search, or add any RSS feed. When a new item matches your rule, Maglev adds it to your downloads. Items that don't match are left alone. Works with any RSS feed. Rules decide what gets added. Watch for a title: Maglev checks every 1, 6 or 24 hours (Wi-Fi only unless you allow mobile data) and tells you when something new turns up.
- An assistant that asks first (optional): Ask in plain words, like "find the latest season of this show in 1080p" or "what's eating my storage?". It searches, compares results, checks size and free space, and shows what it wants to add. Nothing is added or changed until you confirm. Runs on your own OpenRouter key, kept in the phone's secure storage. Can use free models. Keeps working when you switch tabs or leave the app. Chats are saved and come back after a restart. Turn it off and its tab disappears.
- You stay in control: Rules for when and how Maglev downloads, so it fits your data plan, your battery and your storage. Maglev updates itself: a daily check and Check for updates in About. It downloads on Wi-Fi and asks before installing, or installs on its own if you choose. F-Droid and Obtainium installs keep their own updates. The ad block list, search sources and default trackers refresh once a day without an app update, or when you tap Check now. Download only on Wi-Fi, only over a VPN, or only while charging. Pause when the battery runs low. Speed limits for everything or for one download. A schedule for when downloads run or slow down. Pick the files in a torrent and mark one to download first. Pause all, Resume all and Shut down from the notification, and a Quick Settings tile. Files land in Download/Maglev, where any file manager finds them, or in any folder you choose. Move a torrent's files mid-download, and stream video before it finishes. Pauses before the phone runs out of space, keeping 500 MB to 1 GB free, and resumes when space comes back. Backup and restore in Settings: your settings, search sources, torrents and downloads in one file, and your stats if you tick Include stats. API keys are never included. Search your settings from the top of Settings. After an update, a short sheet shows the main new feature, and you can turn it off in Settings > Updates. No analytics or ads SDKs.
- Maglev never gets around DRM. Protected video and live streams can't be saved.
- Release signing certificate SHA-256: c8e15bd47fb39fb2248d8b501a677e61be564d52ba535e31a1608564e35df3c4

## How it works

- Torrents: A modified copy of librqbit, written in Rust, with DHT, trackers, local peer discovery and web seeds.
- Links and streams: The same Rust engine downloads links and stream pieces, keeps resume data next to the file, and checks free space before it starts.
- Browser: Android's own WebView inside a native view that sees every request, so it can block ads and notice the video a player loads. No browser engine is bundled.

## Switching from another app

- [Maglev as an alternative to 1DM+](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/1dm-alternative): Maglev and 1DM+ both download links and torrents with no ads. Maglev is open source under GPL-3.0, reads video links from YouTube, X and Instagram, saves DASH streams as well as HLS, and searches torrent sites from one box. 1DM+ is on Google Play, and Maglev is not there yet.
- [Maglev as an alternative to ADM](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/adm-alternative): Maglev and ADM both download links and torrents, with a browser and a battery cut-off. ADM's Play listing says it contains ads and in-app purchases. Maglev has no ads, and its code is open under GPL-3.0.
- [Maglev as an alternative to LibreTorrent](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/libretorrent-alternative): Maglev runs torrents the way LibreTorrent does, and both are open source under GPL-3.0 with no ads. Maglev also downloads video links and files, and searches torrent sources in one box. LibreTorrent's pages do not list web file downloads or a browser.
- [Maglev as an alternative to Flud](https://harshdayal.dev/maglev/flud-alternative): Maglev and Flud both run torrents, with magnet links, RSS feeds and file selection. Maglev has no ads, and Flud's Google Play listing says it contains ads and in-app purchases. Maglev is open source. Flud's Play page does not say it is.

## FAQ

### Is Maglev free?

Yes. Maglev is free to download and use, with no ads and nothing to buy. It is free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0, made by Harsh Dayal. The source code is public on GitHub, so anyone can check what the app does.

### Does Maglev have ads?

No. Maglev has no ads and no ads SDK. Its built-in browser also blocks ads and trackers on the pages you open, using a list of over 42,000 ad and tracker domains. Once a day Maglev refreshes that list, the search source addresses and the default trackers, from harshdayal.dev/maglev/lists/sources.json and raw.githubusercontent.com, with no cookies and no identifiers. You can replace the list or turn the updates off in Settings.

### Is Maglev safe to install?

Yes, when you get it from the official GitHub Releases page. Maglev is open source, and its release APKs are built by GitHub Actions from the public code. Every official APK is signed with the same key, whose SHA-256 fingerprint is c8e15bd47fb39fb2248d8b501a677e61be564d52ba535e31a1608564e35df3c4. You can check it with apksigner before you install.

### Is it legal to use Maglev?

Yes. Maglev is a download tool, like a browser or download manager; what matters is what you download and your local law. Maglev doesn't host or index any content: its search sends your query to public indexes run by third parties. Download only what you have the right to.

### Does Maglev collect my data or use analytics?

No. Maglev has no analytics or ads SDKs. It contacts only what you use: the sites you open, the block-list addresses in Settings, the public sources you search, the subtitle sources you turn on, and OpenRouter when you use the assistant. Torrents also connect to trackers and other peers, as every torrent client does.

### Why isn't Maglev on the Google Play Store?

Not yet. A Google Play build is planned. Until then, install the APK from GitHub Releases, or add Maglev to Obtainium, which installs new versions from GitHub as they come out.

### Is Maglev available for iPhone?

No. Maglev is an Android app only. It runs on Android 7 and later, on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and emulators. There is no iPhone or iPad version.

### Does Maglev work on Android 7?

Yes. Maglev runs on Android 7 and every later version. On Android 16 and later, download progress also shows as a live chip in the status bar.

### How do I download videos from websites on Android?

Paste or share the page's link to Maglev, pick a quality, and Maglev saves the video. If the site isn't read directly, open the page in Maglev's browser and play the video. Maglev lists it in the Files tray with the page's other files. Tap it to download. Files that need the site's session still work, because Maglev uses the page's cookies for that download.

### How do I save an HLS or m3u8 stream on Android?

Play the video in Maglev's browser, then tap the stream in the Files tray. Choose the quality and audio language and tap Start. Maglev downloads the pieces and joins them into one video file. It saves on-demand HLS and DASH streams, including HLS with standard AES-128 encryption.

### What is a good m3u8 or HLS downloader for Android?

Maglev is one free, open source option. It finds HLS (.m3u8) and DASH streams while a page plays, lets you pick the quality and audio language, and joins the pieces into one video file. It handles on-demand streams, including AES-128 encrypted HLS, and refuses DRM-protected and live streams.

### Which streams can't Maglev save?

DRM-protected streams and live streams, and some players that hide their video inside the page. That includes HLS that uses SAMPLE-AES and Netflix-style protected video. Maglev never gets around DRM, and when it can't save something, it tells you why.

### Can Maglev download YouTube videos?

Yes. Paste or share the link, pick a quality, and Maglev saves the video. Maglev reads it with yt-dlp on your phone and shows up to 6 qualities. It updates yt-dlp by itself once a day on Wi-Fi (Settings > Updates > Video sites). Live streams and Netflix-style protected video can't be saved. A video behind a sign-in may not download, and Maglev says so. See the YouTube downloader guide.

### Can Maglev download subtitles?

Yes, for videos you have already downloaded. Tap Find subtitles on a finished download, or on a video in a torrent's Files tab. Maglev searches 21 free sources with no account and groups the results by how well they fit the file. The subtitle is saved next to the video, so players pick it up. Two sources match by file fingerprint (Subtis for Spanish, Napisy24 for Polish); the rest match by name. Maglev doesn't fetch subtitles by itself when a download finishes.

### Can Maglev download Instagram Reels?

Public Reels and posts, often yes. Paste or share the link, pick a quality, and Maglev reads the video with yt-dlp on your phone. Instagram asks many posts for a sign-in, and those may not download. Maglev says "needs sign-in" when that happens. See the Instagram Reels downloader guide.

### Can Maglev download X (Twitter) videos?

Public videos, often yes. Paste or share the post's link, pick a quality, and Maglev saves the video. A video behind a sign-in may not download, and Maglev says so. See the X (Twitter) video downloader guide.

### Can Maglev download YouTube Shorts?

Yes. Paste or share a Shorts link like any YouTube link and pick a quality. See the YouTube downloader guide.

### Can Maglev save Instagram or X videos?

Yes, for most public videos. Paste or share the link from Instagram, X or another video site and pick a quality. A video behind a sign-in may not download, and Maglev says so. For other pages, open the page in Maglev's browser and play the video: Maglev saves the video files and on-demand HLS or DASH streams it loads. Protected video never saves, so results vary by site and by video.

### Is there an ad-free browser for Android that downloads videos?

Yes, Maglev's built-in browser is one. It blocks ads and trackers before they load, lists the videos and files a page plays or links to, and saves them with the page's cookies. Pop-ups and redirects you didn't tap for wait until you choose Open, Block or Always allow on this site.

### What is a torrent, in plain words?

A torrent is a way to share a file between many people at once. Instead of downloading from one server, your phone gets small pieces from everyone who has the file and shares pieces back while it downloads. A magnet link or a .torrent file tells the app which file to look for.

### Is Maglev a good LibreTorrent or Flud alternative?

It can be. Like LibreTorrent and Flud, Maglev downloads torrents and magnet links and follows RSS feeds. It also downloads video links and files with resume, finds videos on web pages through an ad-free browser, and searches 40 built-in sources. The comparison page lists what each app's own page says.

### Can Maglev open magnet links and .torrent files?

Yes. Open them from your browser, a chat app, the clipboard or a share. You see every file in the torrent before it starts, and you can pick only the ones you want.

### Where can I find torrents to download?

In Maglev's Search tab. One search asks up to 40 built-in public torrent indexes, and merges results that point to the same torrent. Results from sources known for fake uploads carry a warning. You can also add your own Jackett or Prowlarr indexer.

### Which APK file should I download?

You don't have to choose. The Download button picks the right file for your phone. If you want to pick yourself: arm64-v8a is for most phones from the last six years, armeabi-v7a for an older 32-bit phone, x86_64 for an emulator or a Chromebook, and universal if you aren't sure, because it runs on every device.

### What permissions does Maglev need, and why?

Only what downloads need. Notifications show progress and finished downloads. A foreground service and wake lock keep downloads running with the screen off. Network state powers the Wi-Fi-only rule. Storage permission is asked only on Android 9 and older. Maglev can also ask to skip battery optimization and resume downloads after a restart.

### Do I need root or a VPN to use Maglev?

No. Maglev needs no root and no VPN. If you use a VPN, you can tell Maglev to download only while the VPN is connected, and it pauses whenever the VPN drops.

### Can I back up Maglev and restore it on a new phone?

Yes. In Settings > Backup, export one file with your settings, search sources, torrents and downloads, and your stats if you tick Include stats. API keys are never included. On the new phone, open the file in Settings > Backup and choose what to restore.

### Where does Maglev save downloaded files?

In the Download/Maglev folder on your phone, where any file manager can find them. When a download finishes you can open it, share it or open its folder right from the list.

### Can I save downloads to a different folder?

Yes. You can choose any folder for your downloads. You can even move a torrent's files to another folder while it is still downloading.

### Can I pause and resume downloads?

Yes. Pause, resume and retry work for torrents and for links, and they survive a restart. If a link has expired, Maglev asks for a fresh one and continues where it stopped.

### Do downloads keep going in the background?

Yes. Downloads keep going with the screen off. If Android closes the app, Maglev comes back and carries on. The notification has Pause all, Resume all and Shut down buttons.

### Can I download only on Wi-Fi?

Yes. You can set Maglev to download only on Wi-Fi, only when a VPN is on, or only while charging. You can also set speed limits and a schedule for when downloads run or slow down.

### Does Maglev drain the battery?

It uses battery while it downloads, like any download app, and torrents also use it while they share with others. To keep it in check, Maglev can pause on low battery, download only while charging, and stop sharing a torrent once it reaches the ratio or time you set.

### How do I get updates?

Add Maglev to Obtainium and new versions install as they come out. Or download the new APK from GitHub Releases and install it over the old one; your downloads and settings stay.

### Does Maglev check for updates, and what does that send?

Once a day, and when you tap Check for updates, Maglev asks api.github.com for the latest release. GitHub sees your IP address and the app version. Turning off Check automatically in Settings → About stops the daily request. The update file downloads from GitHub's release file servers. By default Maglev downloads updates on Wi-Fi and asks before installing. Pick 'Tell me' to decide each time.

### What does the AI assistant do, and do I need it?

You don't need it. The assistant is optional: it searches, compares results, checks size and free space, and explains problems, and it always waits for you to tap Confirm. It runs on your own OpenRouter key, kept in secure storage, and can use free models. Turn it off and its tab disappears.

### Is Maglev open source?

Yes. Maglev is free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0: you can use, study, change and share it. The source code is on GitHub. The torrent engine is a modified copy of librqbit by Igor Katson, under the Apache License 2.0. Its subtitle sources are ported from the Bazarr+ provider catalog (MIT).

### Is Maglev finished?

Maglev is stable, and it keeps growing: new search sources and features arrive in regular updates. If something goes wrong, please report it on GitHub.

### Who makes Maglev?

Harsh Dayal makes Maglev. You can find him at harshdayal.dev and on GitHub as Kaos599.

### How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?

Open an issue on GitHub. Say what you did, what you expected and what happened, and include your Android version and phone model.
